Everyone knows where the stairs put shoes, in a heap under the east wing.|The stairs have taken another shoe. You suspect they like the taste of yours.|Shoe gone again. You've come to think of the heap under the east wing as a kind of shoe library.} {You have somewhere to be.|It's raining, and the castle floors are cold.|{season == "winter": Your sock is soaked through in a minute.|The stairs grind smugly behind you.}} Go and dig through the heap {You dig through three centuries of shoes and find yours under a buckled pair that must be older than the towers. You're filthy, late and oddly triumphant.|You find your shoe, and a slipper with a name sewn into it from fifty years ago. You leave the slipper on top, in case.|You know the heap's layers now, like a geologist. Your shoe is on top, almost politely. You stub your toe on the way out anyway.} Hop on, one shoe down {You hop to your next lecture and spend it with one foot in your bag. You take excellent notes, out of spite.|You go about your day in one shoe and one sock. People stare; you make the most of it by reading on the move.|You wear one shoe all day, as is becoming your custom. A first-year asks if it's a fashion. You say yes.}
